newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: Two banks seek NZ licences - Radio New Zealand.
newsitem.headline: Two banks seek NZ licences - Radio New Zealand.

text.p: Two foreign investment banks have applied for New Zealand banking licences, Radio New Zealand (RNZ) reported on Tuesday.

Reserve Bank deputy governor Dick Lang had not revealed the names of the banks, but they were understood to be the Bank of Tokyo-Mitsubishi and Deutsche Bank AG, RNZ said. Lang said the two applications are still pending.
If successful, both banks were expected to concentrate on corporate banking, RNZ said.
There are 16 banks holding licences in New Zealand and since the introduction of the present banking licence regime in 1987 there have been 13 licences surrendered.
